headline: FIRST MINING DRILLS 73 g/t GOLD at Duparquet: High-Grade Peak Extends Abitibi Project
snippet: First Mining Gold's 2025 Duparquet campaign returned 15.14 g/t Au over 5.0m — with a 73.40 g/t peak over 1.0m — across the North, South, and newly discovered Minuit zones in Quebec's Abitibi belt; management says results support resource growth ahead of a planned prefeasibility study.

headline: OREZONE HITS 16.1 g/t Au OVER 6.7m at Casa Berardi as 40,000m Drill Program Begins
snippet: Orezone's first drill campaign at its newly acquired Casa Berardi gold mine in Quebec confirms high-grade continuity in the near-surface F160 and F134 zones, with 6.47 g/t Au over 21.5m as the best wide intercept; the company targets 40,000–60,000m of drilling this year, scaling toward 100,000m/yr.

headline: GOLD DROPS TO $4,558, SILVER TO $73 as Hot CPI Builds Case for Fed Rate Hike in 2026
snippet: Gold has retreated roughly 16% from its January all-time high of $5,589 to around $4,558, while silver trades near $73/oz; April CPI at 3.8% — nearly double the Fed's 2% target — has pushed traders to price in a 1-in-3 chance of a 2026 rate hike, with FOMC minutes due today adding to volatility.

headline: SIGMA LITHIUM FIGHTS BRAZIL COURT RULING: Files Appeal, Flags Coordinated Fake News Attack
snippet: Sigma Lithium is contesting a May 17 ruling by a local Brazilian judge that carries a potential US$10M collateral, calling the decision unwarranted and noting a coordinated social media campaign preceded it; the company says legal precedent suggests a multi-year appeals timeline before any payments are due, and operations continue normally.

headline: RUA GOLD AULD CREEK PEA: $42M NPV in NZ Fast-Track Jurisdiction With 19,000m of Drilling Live
snippet: Rua Gold's Auld Creek gold-antimony project in New Zealand's historic Reefton Goldfield delivered a $42M NPV5% base case ($113M at $4,700/oz spot) with AISC of $1,850/oz and a 5.5-year mine life; a fast-track approvals application filed April 20 could compress permitting to months, with a PFS targeted for Q4 2026.

headline: COPPER SINKS TO $6.25/LB on China Demand Miss: Retail Sales, Industrial Output Both Disappoint
snippet: Copper fell to its lowest in nearly two weeks on May 19 as China's retail sales and industrial production both missed forecasts and fixed asset investment unexpectedly contracted, raising doubts about near-term demand from the world's top copper consumer while broader risk-off sentiment compounded the pressure.

headline: CHINA RARE EARTH INDEX COOLS TO 258.7 — Heavy Rare Earth Markets Now Tell a Different Story
snippet: China's official rare earth price index slipped to 258.7 on May 18, retreating from the 300+ peak hit earlier in 2026, while dysprosium (~$123/kg) and terbium (~$897/kg) remain tight for ex-China buyers reportedly paying several multiples of domestic prices — signaling the emergence of two partially decoupled rare earth markets.

headline: SILVER HEADS FOR 6TH STRAIGHT DEFICIT: 67-Million-Oz Gap Persists Despite Solar Demand Thrifting
snippet: The Silver Institute projects a 67 million-ounce supply deficit in 2026 — the sixth consecutive year — as industrial fabrication dips 2% but structural demand from EVs, data centres, and AI infrastructure offsets slower solar-sector absorption; the $73 pullback from the $87 peak doesn't change the underlying supply math.

headline: UTILITIES UNDER-CONTRACTED FOR 13TH YEAR RUNNING: Sprott Calls Pent-Up Uranium Demand a Coiled Spring
snippet: Sprott's Uranium Watch finds spot uranium holding above $100/lb as utilities have failed to contract at replacement rate for a 13th consecutive year, building a forward shortfall that must eventually come to market; with 70 reactors under construction globally and long-term contract talks accelerating, the firm sees deferred procurement returning at scale.

headline: GDX UP 108% IN A YEAR — Gold Miners' Free Cash Flow Yields Now Rival Energy Stocks at 7.5%
snippet: The VanEck Gold Miners ETF has returned 108% year-over-year, outpacing the S&P 500 by more than 80 percentage points, as senior gold miners generate free cash flow yields approaching 7.5% — comparable to energy stocks — leading analysts to argue the equities still offer meaningful leverage over holding bullion directly.
